title: Parity of the Rational Function g(x) = 1 / (x^2 - 1)
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Determine whether the rational function g(x) = 1 / (x^2 - 1) is even, odd, or neither, and explain your reasoning.

steps.title: Check Domain Symmetry and Substitute -x
steps.explanation: The domain R \ {-1, 1} is symmetric about the origin. Substituting -x into the formula gives 1 / ((-x)^2 - 1).
steps.why: A symmetric domain ensures that whenever g(x) is defined, g(-x) is also defined.

steps.title: Simplify the Denominator
steps.explanation: Since (-x)^2 = x^2, the denominator (-x)^2 - 1 equals x^2 - 1, so g(-x) = g(x).
steps.why: Both the numerator 1 and denominator x^2 - 1 are invariant under x -> -x.

steps.title: Conclude Function Parity
steps.explanation: Because g(-x) = g(x) for all x != +/-1, g(x) = 1 / (x^2 - 1) is an even function.
steps.why: The quotient of two even functions is an even function on its domain.
